title: Track which processes open files on your Mac
summary: Use opensnoop to see which applications are opening files in real time. This helps you identify which app is accessing a specific file or directory.

steps.explain: Start tracking all file opens on the system. This shows every file access event in real time.
steps.expect: A stream of lines showing PID, UID, and filename for every file open event.

steps.explain: To track only a specific process by its name, use the -n flag.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the process to track (e.g., Safari, Finder).

steps.expect: Only file opens by the specified process are shown.

steps.explain: To track only a specific process by its PID, use the -p flag.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: The Process ID (PID) of the process to track.

steps.expect: Only file opens by the process with that PID are shown.

steps.explain: To see which processes are opening a specific file, use the -f flag.

placeholders.name: FILE_PATH
placeholders.description: The full path to the file you want to monitor.

steps.expect: Lines showing which processes are opening the specified file.
